claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is a high-entropy alloy suitable as the initial material system.
Pulsed laser deposition can produce a 2-μm-thick MoS2 coating on CoCrFeMnNi.
The deposited MoS2 coating will form a layered surface structure.
The deposited MoS2 layer will have low shear strength.
The low-shear-strength MoS2 layer will accommodate sliding contact without generating high friction forces.
The MoS2 coating will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
The MoS2 coating will act as a sacrificial layer that can wear without damaging the underlying alloy.
The coating will reduce coefficient of friction by at least 40% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The coating will reduce wear rate by at least 60% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The claimed friction and wear reductions will persist from 25°C to 500°C.
The claimed friction and wear reductions will persist at sliding speeds up to 1 m/s.
The claimed friction and wear reductions will persist under normal loads up to 100 N.
The magnitudes of the friction and wear reductions may depend on operating conditions.
The magnitudes of the friction and wear reductions may depend on MoS2 coating quality.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least a 40% friction reduction and a 60% wear-rate reduction, but the falsification rule only rejects the hypothesis if there is no reduction. Results showing smaller positive reductions would violate the quantitative hypothesis without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
